verses.2: Let me speak a little longer, and I will show you, for still there are words left in me.
verses.3: I will take knowledge from afar, and righteousness from my works I will declare.
verses.4: For my words are not false; they are not unjust in their understanding.
verses.5: Know that God does not abandon the innocent; the mighty is strong in heart.
verses.6: He does not give life to the wicked, and the judgment of the poor He gives.
verses.7: He does not turn His eyes from the righteous, and with kings He places them on the throne and exalts them forever.
verses.8: But the bound in fetters are caught in the cords of hardship.
verses.9: And He reveals their deeds and their sins, when they become too great.
verses.10: And He uncovers their ears to discipline, and He says, "Let them return from their wrongdoing."
verses.11: If they listen and serve, they will complete their days in goodness, and their years in pleasantness.
verses.12: But if they do not listen, in His sending they will pass away and perish without knowledge.
verses.13: And the rebellious of heart set their anger, they do not cry out, because He has bound them.
verses.14: So the soul of the young perishes, and their life among the holy ones.
verses.15: He rescues the poor in his poverty, and He uncovers the ears of the oppressed.
verses.16: And He turned you away from the mouth of your enemy — a wide abyss beneath you, and your table descended full of ashes.
verses.17: You are filled with the judgment of the wicked, judgment and justice will uphold you.
verses.18: For wrath, lest He entice you with doubt, and great atonement, let it not turn you aside.
verses.19: Will your ransom not be of use to you in distress, nor all the strong in power?
verses.20: Do not long for the night to rise, for peoples to come against you.
verses.21: Guard yourself, do not turn to wrongdoing, for you have chosen this instead of hardship.
verses.22: Know that the mighty sets Himself apart in His strength — who is like Him, the Teacher?
verses.23: Who has marked His ways for Him, and who has said, "You did wrong"?
verses.24: Remember that His works are great, which men have transgressed.
verses.25: Every person has seen this; a mortal gazes from afar.
verses.26: Know that the mighty cannot be known — His years are uncounted, and no one comprehends.
verses.27: For He draws off the drops of water, they flow as rain to His clouds.
verses.28: From which the streams descend, they surge upon the face of mankind.
verses.29: Even though He spreads out the clouds, He covers the beams of His dwelling.
verses.30: Behold, He spreads light over Himself, and He covers the roots of the sea.
verses.31: For through these He judges peoples, He gives food to the one who hears.
verses.32: With His hands He covers the light, and He commands it over the cloud.
verses.33: He declares it to His friend — the Shepherd, even over what is rising.

notes:
Notes
- v. 13: "the rebellious of heart" — the Hebrew term חַנְפֵי־לֵב is rendered as "rebellious of heart," capturing the sense of a hardened, defiant spirit.
- v. 29: "the beams of His dwelling" — the reference to the "beams" (תְּשֻׁאוֹת) is poetic, likely referring to the architectural structure of God's heavenly dwelling, here rendered as "beams."
- v. 33: "the Shepherd" — the Greek reference to "the Shepherd" is not present in the Hebrew, which uses רֵעוֹ ("friend" or "fellow"). The Hebrew is more neutral, though poetic.

[1] Elihu continued and said:

[2] Let me speak a little longer, and I will show you, for still there are words left in me.

[3] I will take knowledge from afar, and righteousness from my works I will declare.

[4] For my words are not false; they are not unjust in their understanding.

[5] Know that God does not abandon the innocent; the mighty is strong in heart.

[6] He does not give life to the wicked, and the judgment of the poor He gives.

[7] He does not turn His eyes from the righteous, and with kings He places them on the throne and exalts them forever.

[8] But the bound in fetters are caught in the cords of hardship.

[9] And He reveals their deeds and their sins, when they become too great.

[10] And He uncovers their ears to discipline, and He says, "Let them return from their wrongdoing."

[11] If they listen and serve, they will complete their days in goodness, and their years in pleasantness.

[12] But if they do not listen, in His sending they will pass away and perish without knowledge.

[13] And the rebellious of heart set their anger, they do not cry out, because He has bound them.

[14] So the soul of the young perishes, and their life among the holy ones.

[15] He rescues the poor in his poverty, and He uncovers the ears of the oppressed.

[16] And He turned you away from the mouth of your enemy — a wide abyss beneath you, and your table descended full of ashes.

[17] You are filled with the judgment of the wicked, judgment and justice will uphold you.

[18] For wrath, lest He entice you with doubt, and great atonement, let it not turn you aside.

[19] Will your ransom not be of use to you in distress, nor all the strong in power?

[20] Do not long for the night to rise, for peoples to come against you.

[21] Guard yourself, do not turn to wrongdoing, for you have chosen this instead of hardship.

[22] Know that the mighty sets Himself apart in His strength — who is like Him, the Teacher?

[23] Who has marked His ways for Him, and who has said, "You did wrong"?

[24] Remember that His works are great, which men have transgressed.

[25] Every person has seen this; a mortal gazes from afar.

[26] Know that the mighty cannot be known — His years are uncounted, and no one comprehends.

[27] For He draws off the drops of water, they flow as rain to His clouds.

[28] From which the streams descend, they surge upon the face of mankind.

[29] Even though He spreads out the clouds, He covers the beams of His dwelling.

[30] Behold, He spreads light over Himself, and He covers the roots of the sea.

[31] For through these He judges peoples, He gives food to the one who hears.

[32] With His hands He covers the light, and He commands it over the cloud.

[33] He declares it to His friend — the Shepherd, even over what is rising.
